options: How well a model fits its training rows
How well a model performs on new, unseen data from the same source
How many features the model uses
questions.explain: Generalization is performance on data the model was not trained on, and it is the true goal of a model.

questions.q: A straight line is fitted to clearly curved data and misses the pattern on both training and test data. This is mainly a problem of:
questions.explain: A model too simple for the pattern is consistently wrong on all data. That is high bias, or underfitting.

questions.q: In the polynomial experiment, degree 9 had the lowest training error and the highest test error. What does that indicate?
options: The test set was too large
The model is the best of the three
Low bias but high variance, meaning overfitting
questions.explain: Very low training error with much worse test error is the signature of high variance and overfitting.

questions.q: In the refit-on-200-samples experiment, what did the 'spread' (standard deviation) of predictions measure?
options: Variance: how much the prediction changes with the training sample
questions.explain: The spread of predictions across different training samples is variance. The gap between the average prediction and the truth is bias.

questions.q: As you make a model more flexible, what typically happens?
questions.explain: That is the bias-variance tradeoff: more flexibility captures more of the true pattern (less bias) but is more sensitive to the sample (more variance).
